**Surat al-Sajdah (The Chapter of Prostration)**

It is a Meccan surah according to all scholars, except al-Kalbi and Muqatil, who said: "Except for three verses from it, beginning with ﴿Is one who was a believer﴾ to the end of them."

Others said: "Except for five verses, from ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ to ﴿the punishment which you used to deny﴾."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿There is no doubt in it﴾, meaning there is no doubt that it is a revelation ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-rayb (doubt) is the doubt that inclines toward evil and fear. Abu Dhu'ayb said:

They traveled by night, then they heard a sound beyond it,
the rustle of the veil and the knocking of a striking that is struck.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh, who say that Muhammad invented this Qur'an and lies about it.

(p-353) ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is the truth, sent down to you from your Lord.

﴿That you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you﴾, meaning Quraysh. Qatadah said: they were an unlettered nation, and no warner had come to them before Muhammad (ﷺ).

(p-354)

The words of the Exalted, ﴿He arranges the affair﴾, have two interpretations:

First: He decrees the affair. This is the view of Mujahid.

Second: He sends down the revelation. This is the view of al-Suddi.

﴿From the heaven to the earth﴾. Al-Suddi said: from the lowest heaven (samaʾ al-dunya) to the lower earth. On this there are two interpretations:

First: He arranges the affair in the heaven and on the earth.

Second: He arranges it in the heaven, and then the angel descends with it to the earth. Amr ibn Murra narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit that he said: Four angels arrange the affairs of the world: Jibril (Gabriel), Mikail (Michael), the Angel of Death, and Israfil. As for Jibril, he is entrusted with the winds and the hosts. As for Mikail, he is entrusted with rain and water. As for the Angel of Death, he is entrusted with taking souls. As for Israfil, he descends with the command to them.

﴿Then it ascends to Him﴾. On this there are three opinions:

First: It is Jibril, who ascends to the heaven after descending with the revelation. This is the view of Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: It is the angel who arranges the affair, from the heaven to the earth. This is the view of al-Naqqash.

Third: It is the reports of the people of the earth that ascend to Him together with the angels who carry them. This is the view of Ibn Shajara.

﴿In a day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count﴾. On this there are three opinions:

First: He decrees the affair of every thing for a thousand years in one day, then He hands it over to His angels. When that period has passed, He decrees for another thousand years, and so on forever. This is the view of Mujahid.

Second: The angel descends and ascends in a day whose journey is a thousand years. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

Third: The angel descends and ascends in a day whose measure is a thousand years, so that the time of his descent is five hundred years and the time of his ascent is five hundred years. This is the view of Qatada. Thus, according to the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak, the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of a thousand years, and according to the view of Qatada and al-Suddi, it is a journey of five hundred years.

﴿Of what you count﴾, that is, what you reckon from the days of the world. This "day" is an expression for a period measured as a thousand years of the years of the world. It is not a day consisting of daylight between two nights, because with God there is no night of rest nor time of farewell. The Arabs sometimes express the duration of an era by "day," as the poet said:

Two days: a day of stopping at watering places and assemblies, and a day of journeying to the enemies, returning at dusk.

He does not mean two specific days; rather, he meant that their time is divided into two halves, and he expressed each of the two halves by a day.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 32, verses 7–9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾. On this there are five interpretations:

First: He made everything He created good, to the extent that He made even the dog good in its creation. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Second: He made everything He created firm and sound, until He perfected it. This is the view of Mujahid.

Third: He showed kindness to everything that was created, so that its creation was a kindness to it. This is the view of Ali ibn Isa.

Fourth: He inspired what He created with what they need, until they knew it. This comes from their saying, "So-and-so yuhsinu (knows well) such-and-such," meaning he knows it.

Fifth: He gave everything He created what it needs, then guided it to it. This was related by Hamid ibn Qays.

It may also bear a sixth meaning: that He knew everything He created and made it good without learning and without a prior model, so that His power became manifest in it and His wisdom became evident in it.

﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾, meaning Adam. Awn related from Abu Zuhayr, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam from a handful He took from all of the earth. So his descendants came according to the colours of the earth: among them the white and the red, and between those; the easy and the difficult, the evil and the good, and between those."

﴿Then He made his offspring﴾, meaning his progeny, ﴿from an extract﴾ (sulalah), because it is extracted (yansalu) from his loins, ﴿from a despised fluid﴾. Mujahid said: "weak."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He proportioned him﴾. On this there are two views:

One: He proportioned his creation in the womb.

Two: He proportioned his creation as He willed.

﴿And breathed into him of His spirit﴾. On this there are four views:

One: "of His power," as said by Abu Rawq.

Two: "of His progeny," as said by Qatadah.

Three: "of His command, that it should be, and it was," as said by al-Dahhak.

Four: "a spirit from His spirit," that is, from His creation, and He attributed it to Himself because it is from His action. He expressed it with "breathing" because the spirit is of the same kind as wind.

﴿And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts﴾, meaning the hearts. The heart is called fu'ad (inner heart) because it is the source of the innate heat (al-hararah al-ghariziyyah, the natural body heat), derived from the root meaning to be heated, which is the place of fire. He singled out hearing, sight, and the hearts for mention because they are the place of thought and reflection.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَقالُوا أإذا ضَلَلْنا في الأرْضِ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: هَلَكْنا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

الثّانِي: صِرْنا فِيهِ رُفاتًا وتُرابًا، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. والعَرَبُ تَقُولُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ غَيْرُهُ حَتّى خَفِيَ فِيهِ أثَرُهُ: قَدْ ضَلَّ. قالَ الأخْطَلُ:

؎ كُنْتُ القَذى في مَوْجٍ أكْدَرَ مُزْبِدٍ ∗∗∗ تَقْذِفُ الأتِيُّ بِهِ فَضَلَّ ضَلالًا

(I was the speck in a turbid, foaming wave, which the flood tossed about, so it was lost, utterly lost.)

الثّالِثُ: غُيِّبْنا في الأرْضِ، قالَهُ قُطْرُبٌ، وأنْشَدَ النّابِغَةُ:

؎ فَآبَ مُضِلُّوهُ بِعَيْنٍ جَلِيَّةٍ ∗∗∗ وغُودِرَ بِالجَوَلانِ حَزْمٌ ونائِلُ

(So his pursuers returned with a clear sign, while Hazm and Na'il were left behind at al-Jawlan.)

وَقَرَأ الحَسَنُ: ﴿صَلَلْنا﴾ بِصادٍ غَيْرِ مُعْجَمَةٍ، وفِيهِ عَلى قِراءَتِهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أيْ أنْتَنَتْ لُحُومُنا، مِن قَوْلِهِمْ صَلَّ اللَّحْمُ إذا أنْتَنَ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ.

(p-357) الثّانِي: صَلَلْنا مِنَ الصَّلَّةِ، وهي الأرْضُ اليابِسَةُ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿مِن صَلْصالٍ كالفَخّارِ﴾. ﴿أإنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ أيْ أتُعادُ أجْسامُنا لِلْبَعْثِ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا، تَعَجُّبًا مِن إعادَتِها وإنْكارًا لِبَعْثِهِمْ، وهو مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿بَلْ هم بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ كافِرُونَ﴾. وقِيلَ إنَّ قائِلَ ذَلِكَ أُبَيُّ بْنُ خَلَفٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قُلْ يَتَوَفّاكم مَلَكُ المَوْتِ الَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ﴾ أيْ يَقْبِضُ أرْواحَكم. والتَّوَفِّي: أخْذُ الشَّيْءِ عَلى تَمامٍ، مَأْخُوذٌ مِن تَوْفِيَةِ العَدَدِ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُمُ: اسْتَوْفَيْتُ دَيْنِي مِن فُلانٍ.

ثُمَّ في تَوَفِّي مَلَكِ المَوْتِ لَهم قَوْلانِ:

الأوَّلُ: بِأعْوانِهِ.

الثّانِي: بِنَفْسِهِ.

رَوى جَعْفَرٌ الصّادِقُ عَنْ أبِيهِ قالَ: «نَظَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) إلى مَلَكِ المَوْتِ عِنْدَ رَأْسِ رَجُلٍ مِنَ الأنْصارِ، فَقالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ): [يا مَلَكَ المَوْتِ]: (ارْفُقْ بِصاحِبِي فَإنَّهُ مُؤْمِنٌ). فَقالَ مَلَكُ المَوْتِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ: يا مُحَمَّدُ، طِبْ نَفْسًا وقَرَّ عَيْنًا، فَإنِّي بِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ رَفِيقٌ. واعْلَمْ أنَّ ما مِن أهْلِ بَيْتِ مَدَرٍ ولا شَعْرٍ إلّا وأنا أتَصَفُّحُهم في كُلِّ يَوْمٍ خَمْسَ مَرّاتٍ، حَتّى لَأنا أعْرَفُ بِصَغِيرِهِمْ وكَبِيرِهِمْ مِنهم بِأنْفُسِهِمْ. واللَّهِ يا مُحَمَّدُ لَوْ أنِّي أرَدْتُ أنْ أقْبِضَ رُوحَ بَعُوضَةٍ ما قَدَرْتُ عَلى ذَلِكَ حَتّى يَكُونَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هو الآمِرَ بِقَبْضِها».

قالَ جَعْفَرٌ: إنَّما يَتَصَفَّحُهم عِنْدَ مَواقِيتِ الصَّلَواتِ.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 32, verses 12–14:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord﴾, i.e., before the reckoning of their Lord. Concerning this there are four opinions:

First: out of grief. This was said by Ibn Isa.

Second: out of humiliation. This was said by Ibn Shajara.

Third: out of shame. This was related by al-Naqqash.

Fourth: out of regret. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

﴿Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: we have seen the truth of Your threat and we have heard the confirmation of Your messengers. This was said by Ibn Isa.

The second: we have seen our disobedience and we have heard what was said about us. Qatada said: they saw when sight no longer benefited them, and they heard when hearing no longer benefited them.

﴿So return us, that we may work righteousness; indeed we are certain﴾, i.e., return us to the world, that we may work righteousness in it.

﴿Indeed we are certain﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: we affirm the Resurrection. This was said by al-Naqqash.

The second: we affirm that what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought is true. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

Sufyan said: Allah then refuted them, saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28], and the verse.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

First: its guidance to faith.

Second: to Paradise.

Third: its guidance in returning to the world, because they asked for a return in order to believe.

﴿But the word from Me has come into effect﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: its meaning is that the word from Me has preceded. This was said by al-Kalbi and Yahya ibn Sallam.

Two: the word from Me has become binding. This was said by al-Suddi, as Kathir said:

*"If there is reproach, then welcome and ease; the reproach has come due for her, and it has been brief in this world."*

﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men﴾, meaning: whoever among the jinn and men disobeyed Him.

Concerning "the jinn" there are two opinions:

First: that it refers to the jinn. This was said by Ibn Kamil.

Second: that they are the angels. This was related by al-Suddi from Ikrima, but this interpretation is flawed, because the angels do not disobey Allah so as to be punished.

They were called jinn because they are hidden from sight (ijtinan), and from this is the saying of Zayd ibn Amr:

*"The jinn and the gardens have been removed from me, and thus does the steadfast, patient one act."*

Allah's words: ﴿So taste, for your forgetting the meeting of this your day. Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

First: "Taste My punishment because you abandoned My command." Said by al-Dahhak.

Second: "Taste the punishment because you abandoned belief in the Resurrection on this day." Said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

First: We have left you from good. Said by al-Suddi.

Second: We have left you in punishment. Said by Mujahid.

﴿And taste the punishment of eternity﴾, which is the everlasting one that has no cessation.

﴿For what you used to do﴾, meaning in the world, of sins. The word "taste" may be used for what befalls the soul even if it is not something eaten, because the soul perceives it just as it perceives the taste of food. Ibn Abi Rabi'a said:

*"Taste its abandonment, if you claim that it is right guidance; O Lord, the claim has not been false."*

﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ has two interpretations:

One: from His worship. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: from prostration, as the people of Makkah were arrogant about prostrating to Him. This was related by al-Naqqash.

One: for the remembrance of Allah, whether in prayer or outside prayer. This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

(p-362) The second: for prayer. (p-363) Regarding the prayer for which their sides forsake their beds, there are four sayings:

First: voluntary prayer between Maghrib and Isha. This was said by Qatada and Ikrimah.

Second: the Isha prayer, which is called the prayer of 'Atama. This was said by al-Hasan and Ata.

Third: the Subh and Isha prayers in congregation. This was said by Abu al-Darda and Ubada.

Fourth: the night vigil. This was said by Mujahid, al-Awza'i, Malik and Ibn Zayd.

One: in fear of His reckoning and hope for His mercy.

The second: in fear of His punishment and hope for His reward.

It may also admit a third meaning: they call upon Him to ward off what they fear and to seek what they hope for, and they do not turn away from Him in fear or in hope.

﴿and from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ has four interpretations:

One: they give zakat, seeking its reward. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: voluntary charity beyond zakat. This was said by Qatada.

The third: spending in obedience to Allah. Qatada said: "Spend from what Allah has given you, for these wealths are loans and deposits with you, O son of Adam; you are about to part with them."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 32, verses 18–22:

Allah's words: ﴿Is then one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner?﴾ The believer here is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him), and the defiant sinner is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿUqba reviled ʿAlī and said, "I am broader than you in tongue, sharper than you in spear, and fuller than you in filling." ʿAlī (may Allah honour his face) said to him, "It is not as you have said, O defiant one." So this verse was revealed concerning the two of them.

﴿They are not equal﴾. Qatada said: "No, by Allah, they are not equal, neither in this world, nor at death, nor in the Hereafter."

Allah's words: ﴿And We will surely make them taste a nearer punishment short of the greater punishment﴾. As for the nearer punishment, it is in this world, and concerning it there are seven opinions:

The first: it is the calamities of this world affecting the self and wealth. This was said by Ubayy.

The second: killing by the sword. This was said by Ibn Masʿūd.

The third: that it is the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās.

The fourth: famine and drought. This was said by Ibrahim (al-Nakhaʿi).

The fifth: the punishment of the grave. This was said by al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib and Mujāhid.

The sixth: that it is the punishment of the whole world. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The seventh: that it is the high cost of prices, and the greater punishment is the emergence of the Mahdi. This was said by Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq.

It may also be understood as an eighth: that the nearer punishment is in wealth, the greater is in the self, and the greater punishment is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.

﴿So that they may return﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: they return to the truth. This was said by Ibrahim.

The second: they repent from disbelief. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās.

The root of juruz is cessation, derived from their saying: a sword that is jurraz, meaning one that cuts; and a she-camel that is jurraz, meaning one that eats everything, because she leaves nothing without cutting it with her mouth.

A man may be described as jarur, meaning a voracious eater. The poet (al-Rajiz) said:

Grain that is devoured; when it is hungry it weeps, it eats dates and does not spit out the pits.

(p-368) Ibn Ata interpreted this verse to mean that the blessings of admonitions reach hardened hearts.

﴿To the barren land﴾. Concerning it there are five sayings:

The first: it is the dry land, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: it is the land that has consumed what was in it of crops and trees, said by Ibn Shajara.

The third: it is the land that receives water only from torrents, said by Ibn Abbas.

The fourth: it is the land of Aden-Abyan that does not produce plants, said by Mujahid.

The fifth: it is the villages of Nabya between Yemen and Syria, said by al-Hasan.

The root of juruz is cessation, derived from their saying: a sword that is jurraz, meaning one that cuts; and a she-camel that is jurraz, meaning one that eats everything, because she leaves nothing without cutting it with her mouth.

A man may be described as jarur, meaning a voracious eater. The poet (al-Rajiz) said:

Grain that is devoured; when it is hungry it weeps, it eats dates and does not spit out the pits.

(p-368) Ibn Ata interpreted this verse to mean that the blessings of admonitions reach hardened hearts.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 32, verses 28–30:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When is this victory?"﴾ Concerning this there are three opinions:

The first: It is the conquest of Makkah. This was said by al-Farra'.

The second: The victory has passed by their punishment in this world. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: The judgment with reward and punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Mujahid.

al-Hasan said: Allah did not send any prophet except that he warned against the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

﴿Say, "On the day of victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them."﴾ Concerning this there are three opinions:

The first: They are those from the Banu Kinanah whom Khalid ibn al-Walid killed on the day of the conquest of Makkah. This was said by al-Farra'.

The second: The day of victory is the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Mujahid.

The third: It is the day on which the punishment will come upon them. This was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

﴿And they will not be given respite﴾, i.e., they will not be delayed in punishment when the time comes.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, the verse.

Qatadah said: It was revealed before he was commanded to fight them. It may bear three meanings:

The first: Turn away from their harm and await their punishment.

The second: Turn away from fighting them and await permission for you to wage jihad against them.

The third: Turn away by emigrating and await what Allah will supply you with of support. And Allah knows best.
